# Named Character Classes

This reference uses the bundled Unicode 18.0.0 data and the exact registry used by the Legs parser.
Regenerate it from the repository root with `make gen-grammars`.

Names are case-sensitive and begin with `$`: `$Letter`, `$L` and `$Ascii_Letter` are examples.
Each reference matches one character; add `+` to match a run.
References denote character sets, not other pattern definitions.

Inside brackets, juxtaposition forms a union, `&` an intersection, `-` a difference, and `^` a symmetric difference.
For example, `[$Ascii_Letter _]` includes ASCII letters and underscore; `[$Letter - $Ascii]` excludes ASCII letters.
Use nested brackets to make grouping explicit.
The escape `\s` means a literal ASCII space, not a Unicode whitespace class.

Category aliases include short codes, full names and unambiguous first words.
`Decimal` is the exception: it is the ASCII convenience class 0-9, not an alias of `Decimal_Number`/`Nd`.
ASCII category subsets have names such as `Ascii_Letter` and aliases such as `AL`; empty subsets are omitted.
Block names describe code-point intervals, including any unassigned positions within them.
Plane classes cover the bundled block ranges rounded to 4096-code-point boundaries, excluding surrogates;
they do not necessarily cover every position in a plane.
Surrogate classes are listed in the registry but cannot match valid UTF-8 input.

Convenience classes include `Binary`/`Bin` (0-1), `Quaternary`/`Quat` (0-3), `Octal`/`Oct` (0-7),
`Decimal`/`Dec` (0-9), and `Hexadecimal`/`Hex` (0-9, A-F, a-f).
`Visible`/`V` combines L, M, N, P and S; `Readable`/`R` also includes Z.
`Ascii_Visible`/`AV` and `Ascii_Readable`/`AR` restrict those sets to ASCII.
`Control_0`/`C0` covers U+0000-U+001F; `Control_1`/`C1` covers U+0080-U+009F.
`Ascii`/`A` covers U+0000-U+007F. `Other_Encodable`/`CE` is category C without surrogates.

The table lists every accepted name. Counts include all code points in the class, including unencodable surrogates.
Interval endpoints are inclusive.
